top_choice_rationale: Can Xue (P001) remains my first choice on literary grounds. Her dream-logic fiction, as named on the list in Frontier and Love in the New Millennium, has a distinctive voice and a formal principle that replaces conventional psychology, space and causal plot. It is a kept method, not decorative surrealism. It has been pursued over decades, and the compression of the work makes repetition cost less than in very long cycles. The citation rests on the fiction and the single-writer scope is clean. This is a close and provisional judgment. The open question is whether the method deepens or only restates itself, and whether the novels hold up as well as the stories. No specific reading in the exchange has answered it. I also cannot judge the Chinese original, only part of her large output is available in translation, and I have not independently verified any text. Agreement among colleagues is not an independent check, since we share the same translated sample. Cărtărescu (P002) is a serious and close second, with a citation centred on the novels. I would move him first if the later Can Xue novels were shown to restate the early method. Both are preferred to no award (P000), which I rank last because two substantial recommendations are available.
